_comment: A24 (owner, 2026-10-06), signed 2026-10-08 by Andrew Azelton. Junctional-specific lines served at the top of the DCR card's DO THIS when the medic's question states junctional bleeding (groin, axilla, neck), each with verbatim corpus quotes. Owner's decisions at signing: the DCR in PFC CPG cited as ID73 (01 Oct 2018; rapid updates to 01 Sep 2023) and CCATT NPWT as ID49 (rev. 26 Feb 2025), both as the corpus prints them; line 3 (manual pressure) kept as cited, its source being aeromedical care of a non-life-threatening junctional bleed; TCCC's 3 minutes of direct pressure left out (not in the corpus); the 2-hour conversion confirmed junctional in the source (ID73 p.5). If a line's text changes, the owner re-signs (nothing in code enforces this; the A24b test pins the signed text word for word).
sites: groin / inguinal, axilla / armpit, neck (cervical): JTS CPG ID82 p.13

do_this.text: Junctional bleeding (groin, axilla, neck): pack the wound tightly with a hemostatic dressing (Combat Gauze, Celox Gauze, ChitoGauze; XStat for a deep wound) and put a pressure dressing over it.

sources.citation: JTS CPG ID73, Damage Control Resuscitation in Prolonged Field Care (01 Oct 2018; rapid updates to 01 Sep 2023)
sources.quote: • Limb tourniquets • Wound packing • Pressure dressings • Hemostatic dressings • Junctional tourniquets • Pelvic binders

sources.citation: JTS CPG ID73, Damage Control Resuscitation in Prolonged Field Care (01 Oct 2018; rapid updates to 01 Sep 2023)
sources.quote: Pressure dressings  Hemostatic dressings (Combat Gauze, Celox Gauze, Chito Gauze, and XStat  Junctional tourniquets  Pelvic binders

sources.citation: JTS CPG ID18, Damage Control Resuscitation (12 Jul 2019)
sources.quote: and the XSTAT™ device, which injects absorbent sponges into deep wounds to tamponade bleeding.

sources.citation: CCATT CPG ID49, Negative Pressure Wound Therapy during Aeromedical Evacuation (rev. 26 Feb 2025)
sources.quote: pack the wound tightly and apply a pressure dressing to the entire limb.

do_this.text: Groin or axilla: apply a junctional tourniquet if one is carried (Combat Ready Clamp, SAM Junctional Tourniquet, Junctional Emergency Treatment Tool).

sources.citation: JTS CPG ID18, Damage Control Resuscitation (12 Jul 2019)
sources.quote: Junctional (axillary, neck, and groin) hemorrhage, previously a nearly intractable problem, can now be treated with approved junctional tourniquets (e.

sources.citation: JTS CPG ID18, Damage Control Resuscitation (12 Jul 2019)
sources.quote: , Combat Ready Clamp, SAM® Junctional Tourniquet, Junctional Emergency Treatment Tool)

do_this.text: Until it is on, or if none is carried, hold firm manual pressure on the packed wound.

sources.citation: CCATT CPG ID49, Negative Pressure Wound Therapy during Aeromedical Evacuation (rev. 26 Feb 2025)
sources.quote: maintain manual pressure using a team member rather than converting to a junctional tourniquet as manual pressure may be more reliable.

watch.text: Junctional tourniquet on: transition to a pressure dressing within 2 hours when the criteria for conversion are met.

sources.citation: JTS CPG ID73, Damage Control Resuscitation in Prolonged Field Care (01 Oct 2018; rapid updates to 01 Sep 2023)
sources.quote: Tourniquets (limb and junctional) should be transitioned to pressure dressings within 2 hours when criteria for conversion are met
